result.title: Shallow Probes Are Sufficient for Near-Oracle Personalization Depth Allocation in Federated Learning
result.comment: 6 pages, 9 figures. Accepted and presented at SINCONF 2026 (18th International Conference on Security of Information and Networks), Beykent University, Istanbul, Turkiye, 14-16 October 2026
result.summary: Rather than proposing a new federated optimizer, we study whether a small client-specific measurement budget can support cost-aware personalization-depth decisions under a utility that trades Macro-F1 against deployment cost. Exhaustive evaluation of six depths defines an offline oracle that is not deployable. We audit the Probe Sufficiency Hypothesis: three shallow probes (P0--P2) may contain most decision-relevant information for approaching that oracle. FedPBA is a secondary learned instantiation for deep-action extrapolation. On CIFAR-10/100 and patient-disjoint PTB-XL (45 sessions; 900 clients; 2700 evaluations; GroupKFold), training-free greedy probing achieves regret 0.0071 and 98.3 percent oracle recovery, beating metadata-only policies and FedPBA (0.0110 / 97.3 percent). Aggregate shallow-best versus oracle correlation is 0.9818 but falls to 0.578 on deep-oracle rows; PTB-XL deep-oracle cases remain a high-regret boundary without a validated escalation gate.

AI.brief_summary: 论文考察联邦学习中在成本-效用权衡下，少量浅层探针（P0–P2）是否足以支撑每客户端的个性化深度分配决策以逼近离线 oracle，并在 CIFAR-10/100 与 PTB-XL 上比较无训练贪心探测、仅元数据策略与 FedPBA。
AI.relevance_reason: 「浅层探测能否含足够决策信息以决定是否深入」与 LVR 的 STOP 决策、动态计算预算分配可能有概念联系，可供核查浅层状态是否足以预测更深的推理深度；但领域与多模态推理相距较远，属推测性借鉴。
